use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

claims.content: The C2 JU publishes air and surface surveillance tracks to ensure the exchange of complete, accurate, and timely surveillance information for joint operations while minimizing dual designations.

goal.raw_text: The C2 JU publishes air and surface surveillance tracks to ensure the exchange of complete, accurate, and timely surveillance information for joint operations while minimizing dual designations.

claims.content: C2 JU

The C2 JU initiates the publication of air and surface surveillance tracks when there is a requirement to exchange surveillance information and data usable in providing threat warning information among systems involved in joint operations.

claims.content: The C2 JU ensures that surveillance track information exchanged is as complete, accurate, and timely as possible, and that data are correlated to minimize dual designation.
The C2 JU follows proper reporting rules, including providing the source of track data (Source TN) and reporting the position of real-time tracks extrapolated to the time of transmission.
After initially achieving Active status or returning to it, the C2 JU waits a minimum of 12 seconds before transmitting air and surface tracks to allow for responsibility checks and correlation.

If the C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported are eligible for correlation (dual designation), it initiates action to resolve the dual designation, potentially by transmitting a J7.2 Correlation message.
If operational necessity requires it, the C2 JU may override the minimum 12-second wait time before transmitting tracks, or eliminate the wait entirely.

When the C2 JU initiates a J7.2 Correlation message to resolve a dual designation, receiving IUs may reject the requested correlation under certain prespecified conditions, in which case a J7.2 message with Response Value (RV) set to 2 is transmitted to report the rejection.

If a correlation is found between a received PPLI report and a local track for which the C2 JU has reporting responsibility (R²), the JU transmits a J7.2 Correlation message with RV=1 (Reverse Correlation Not Acceptable), ceases reporting the surveillance track, and transmits a J7.0 Drop Track message.

If a correlation is found between a received PPLI report and a track held by another C2 JU with R², and the Track Numbers (TNs) are different, the JU transmits a J7.2 (RV=1) Correlation message identifying the PPLI TN as retained and the surveillance TN as dropped.
If receiving IUs reject a requested correlation under prespecified conditions, they transmit a J7.2 message with Response Value (RV) set to 2 to report the rejection, exiting the correlation attempt.

If a C² JU finds correlation between a received PPLI report and a local track for which it has R², it transmits J7.2 (RV=1), ceases reporting the surveillance track, and sends J7.0 Drop Track message — exiting further reporting of that track.
If a system does not receive a J7.0 (ACT=0) message and receives no further updates on a remote track, it may purge the remote track from its database as an exception handling measure.

Automatic correlation is restricted if tracks have Identity (ID) conflict, different Mode II codes (with local code current), both are locally derived real-time tracks, or either has Strength > 1 — requiring manual intervention or inhibition via operator-selectable capability.
Surveillance track information exchanged is as complete, accurate, and timely as possible.
Data are correlated to minimize dual designation.
